overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to specifically identify the litigation matters in notices and announcements for the February 8 and March 1 executive sessions; other allegations were rejected or not reached.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the January 18, January 25 and February 8 executive sessions cited the wrong purpose and should have been held under Purpose 1 (personnel discipline).
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee’s discussions held in executive session on January 18, January 25, and February 8 related to litigation strategy and were therefore appropriate under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the superintendent was not given the written 48-hour notice required for a Purpose 1 session, and that personnel discipline could only be discussed under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: When a discussion may properly be held under multiple executive session purposes, a public body may choose which executive session purpose or purposes to cite.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the February 8 and March 1 executive session notice topics failed to identify the separate litigation matters (arbitration and MCAD complaint) to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the specific litigation matters to be discussed in executive session on February 8 and March 1.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the chair's open-session announcements before the February 8 and March 1 executive sessions did not identify the specific litigation matters to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to sufficiently identify, both in the notices and in the open session announcements, the litigation matters to be discussed in executive session on February 8 and March 1.

allegations.summary: Complaints demanded more detail, such as whether the arbitration was ongoing and whether the MCAD matter was new or previously discussed; the AG found this detail was not required.
Complaint challenged the sufficiency of litigation notice topics and announcements for the January 18 and January 25 sessions.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the January 18 and 25 meetings, we do not review whether the executive session notice topics and announcements related to litigation matters were sufficient as no complaint clearly raised this allegation with respect to those two meetings.

allegations.summary: A second complaint alleged an unrelated March 1 executive session discussion was improper, but the complainant withdrew it before filing with the AG.
allegations.key_passage: Prior to filing the complaint with our office, the Complainant withdrew this allegation; therefore, we do not address the allegation here.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation).
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
